args: Order-to-payment gap re-measured with refund-inclusive payment status

How much of the gap between order value and 'captured' payments is really just that refunded/partially-refunded payments were excluded by my status filter, versus a genuine hole where money was never collected?

{"run": "run6", "manager": "data", "analyst": "Yuki Tanaka", "engineer": "Bea", "situation": "metric-certification", "week": 1, "night": 3, "request": 1, "grain": "order status", "columns_requested": ["order_status", "order_count", "orders_grand_total_eur", "orders_with_money_collected_count", "gross_collected_eur", "net_collected_eur", "gap_vs_gross_eur", "gap_vs_gross_pct"], "details": "Same population as the prior order-status report: orders with placed_at between 2023-01-01 and 2025-06-30 inclusive. Group by orders.status. order_count and orders_grand_total_eur as before (grand_total converted to EUR via exchange_rates using orders.currency_code and placed_at date). orders_with_money_collected_count = count of those orders with at least one linked payments row (payments.order_id = orders.id) whose status is in ('captured','refunded','partially_refunded') - i.e. any payment that was successfully captured at some point, whether or not it was later refunded. gross_collected_eur = sum of payments.amount for those linked payments (the original captured amount, before any refund), converted to EUR via payments.currency_code and captured_at date. net_collected_eur = sum of (payments.amount - payments.amount_refunded) for those same linked payments, converted the same way - this is what the merchant actually kept after refunds. gap_vs_gross_eur = orders_grand_total_eur - gross_collected_eur. gap_vs_gross_pct = gap_vs_gross_eur / orders_grand_total_eur * 100, rounded to 1 decimal. Tables: orders, payments, exchange_rates. Order by orders_grand_total_eur descending.", "builds_on": ["Order-to-payment gap by order status, aged cohort"]}
